evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth/password_reset.rs: change_password handler (defined at L396, body ends L540) updates the password hash but never calls session_repo.revoke_all_user_tokens(user.id, _).

Sibling reset_password handler in the same file calls state.session_repo.revoke_all_user_tokens(user.id, None) at L345 after persisting the new hash, with comment '// Revoke all refresh tokens for security (force re-login)'.

Impact: after a deliberate password change via POST /api/v1/auth/password/change, every previously-issued refresh token / session on every other device remains valid, defeating the main security purpose of a signed-in password change.

Issue #3352 surfaced this via ppt-review-merged (post-merge review of PR #3348). Repository method session.rs:191 `pub async fn revoke_all_user_tokens(user_id, except)` already exists and is used by reset_password, suspend_cascade, sessions revoke endpoints.

Fix: mirror reset_password's call after user_repo.update_password succeeds; regression test in backend/servers/api-server/tests/suites/auth_tests.rs — refresh with a pre-change refresh token must 401.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/widgets/WidgetDataProvider.ts:373-380 — private apiRequest<T>() wraps the whole fetch in try/catch and, on ANY error, returns `{} as T` instead of re-throwing. Empty-object cast masks the failure from every caller.

Consequence: updateAllWidgets() L136-160 relies on exceptions to classify widget success/failure; because apiRequest never throws, the failure path is dead code — a failed backend fetch resolves to an empty payload, is treated as success, and gets written to AsyncStorage via cacheWidgetData, OVERWRITING previously-valid cached widget data during a backend outage.
Fix vector: remove the `{} as T` fallback so updateAllWidgets' existing success/failure handling engages and good cache is preserved on failure.
